questions.question: Two trains are running on opposite tracks between stations A and B. After crossing each other they take 4 hr and 9 hr respectively to reach their destination. If speed of first train is 54 kmph, find the speed of second train.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Two trains are running on opposite tracks between stations A and B.

After crossing each other they take 4 hr and 9 hr respectively to reach their destination.

Speed of first train is 54 kmph.

**Formula used:**

After crossing each other, if time taken by 2 trains is T1 and T2 resp. then, S1/S2 = √T2/√T1

where, S1 and S2 are speeds of first and second train respectively

**Calculation:**

We have, T1 = 4hr, T2 = 9hr, S1 = 54 kmph

⇒ 54/ S2 = √[9/4] = 3/2

⇒ S2 = 54 × 2 × 1/3 = 36 kmph

⇒ Speed of second train = 36 kmph

Also, time taken to cross each other = √(T1 × T2) = √(9 × 4) = 6 hrs 

Total distance = 54 × 6 + x × 6 = x × 9 + 54 × 4

⇒ 9x - 3x = 54 × (6 - 2)

⇒ 6x = 216

⇒ x = 36 kmph = Speed of second train

questions.question: If x = 7 + 4√3 and y = 2(√x) then find the square of (√x - √y).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

x = 7 + 4√3

y = 2(√x)

**Formulae used:**

(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²

**Calculations:**

x = 7 + 4√3

⇒ x = 7 + 2 × 2 × √3

⇒ x = (2)² + 2 × 2 × √3 + (√3)²

From algebraic identity

⇒ x = (2 + √3)²

⇒ √x = 2 + √3

y = 2(√x) 

⇒ y = 2 × (2 + √3)

⇒ y = 4 + 2 × √3

⇒ y = (√3)² + 2 × √3 × 1 + (1)²

From algebraic identity

⇒ y = (√3 + 1)²

⇒ √y = √3 + 1

Value of √x – √y = 2 + √3 – (√3 + 1)

⇒ 2 + √3 – √3 – 1

⇒ 1

Square of (√x – √y) = (1)² = 1

**∴ Square of (√x – √y) = 1**

questions.question: Seven years from now Virat will be twice as old as Mohinder. Five years ago, Mohinder’s age was one year less than 2/5 of Virat’s age. What is Virat’s present age?
questions.solution:
Let ages of Virat and Mohinder be A and B years respectively.

Seven years from now Virat will be twice as old as Mohinder,

⇒ (A + 7) = 2(B + 7)

⇒ A – 2B = 7

Five years ago, Mohinder’s age was one year less than 2/5 of Virat’s age,

⇒ (B – 5) = 2/5(A – 5) – 1

⇒(B - 5) = (2A - 10 - 5)/(5)

⇒ 5B - 25 = 2A - 15

⇒ 2A – 5B = -10

⇒ 2(7 + 2B) – 5B = -10

⇒ B = 24

⇒ A = 7 + 48 = 55

∴ Virat’s age is 55 years.

questions.question: On which principle does the hydraulic lift works?
questions.solution:
• Hydraulic lift works on the principle of **Pascal's law**.
 
• Pascal's law states that a pressure change occurring anywhere in a confined incompressible fluid is transmitted throughout the fluid such that the same change occurs everywhere.
 
• This law is used in hydraulic lifts and hydraulic brakes in cars.
 
• Archimedes Principle: When a solid body is partially are completely immersed in a fluid, the fluid exerts an upward force on the body, whose magnitude is equal to the weight of the displaced fluid.

questions.question: In a capitalist society the goods produced are distributed among people ______.

options.text: only on the basis of what people need
on the basis of what people need and on the basis of Purchasing Power
not on the basis of Purchasing Power
not on the basis of what people need but on the basis of Purchasing Power

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**not on the basis of what people need but on the basis of Purchasing Power**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a capitalist society, goods are distributed **not on the basis of what people need but on the basis of Purchasing Power**.
 
• Purchasing Power refers to the financial ability of individuals to buy goods and services.
 
• This system often leads to inequalities where those with higher purchasing power can afford more goods and services, while those with less purchasing power may struggle to meet their basic needs.
 
• The principle of distribution based on purchasing power is fundamental to the functioning of a capitalist economy.

questions.question: In what time does a sum of money amount to twice of itself at the simple interest of 25% per annum?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If a sum becomes **n** times of itself at Simple Interest rate **R%**, the time **T** is given by:

T = [(n − 1) × 100] ÷ R

Here, n = 2 (since it becomes twice) and R = 25%.

⇒ T = [(2 − 1) × 100] ÷ 25

⇒ T = 100 ÷ 25 = 4 years

**∴ The correct answer is 4 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Rate of Interest (R) = 25% per annum

Let the Principal (P) be 100 units.

Since the sum amounts to twice itself, Amount (A) = 2 × 100 = 200 units.

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = Amount − Principal

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
 
• 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Start (t = 0)
 End (t = ?)
 
 P = 100 units
 A = 200 units
 
 
 

 

 
 
 SI = +100 units
 Rate = 25% p.a.

**Calculation:**

⇒ SI = 200 − 100 = 100 units

⇒ 100 = (100 × 25 × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 100 = 25 × T

⇒ T = 100 ÷ 25

⇒ T = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum becoming 'n' times (Rate Calculation)

If a sum becomes 'n' times of itself in 'T' years at simple interest, the rate can be found directly by: R = [(n − 1) × 100] ÷ T.

Direct Amount Formula for SI

The total amount A after T years can be calculated as: A = P × [1 + (R × T) ÷ 100].

Rule of 72

A general financial shortcut used to estimate the time required to double an investment when the interest is compounded: Time ≈ 72 ÷ R. However, for Simple Interest, the exact doubling time is always 100 ÷ R.

questions.question: Water vascular system is found in
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Echinodermata**.

__**Explanation-**__

**Echinoderms**, a group that includes sea stars (starfish), sea cucumbers, sea urchins, sand dollars, and brittle stars, possess a unique structural feature known as the water vascular system.

The water vascular system is a network of water-filled canals that function in locomotion, feeding, gas exchange, and sensory perception. Here's how it generally works:

__
 
• **Water Inflow:** Seawater enters the system through a sieve-like structure on the echinoderm's body surface called the** madreporite.**
 
• **Stone Canal:** From the madreporite, water then flows into a short canal, often lined with calcareous material, known as the stone canal.
 
• **Ring Canal**: The stone canal leads to a circular canal, the ring canal, that surrounds the esophagus.
 
• **Radial Canal(s):** Connected to the ring canal are five (or multiples of five) radial canals. These extend into each of the echinoderm's arms (if arms are present).
 
• **Tube Feet:** Off of the radial canals are many lateral canals, each terminating in a muscular, often sucker-tipped, extension known as a tube foot or podium. The sequential contraction and expansion of the tube feet, controlled by the water pressure within the canals, assist with locomotion, enable feeding, and facilitate gas exchange.

The water vascular system in echinoderms allows these marine animals to move effectively despite having no centralized brain nor discernable front or back to their bodies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6b7eee76316bdfbc57ea2bb7c5fa0539a3f0afe6737edf805c5e79ab07de9cd8.png] 

**Conclusion-**__ Water vascular system is observed in Echinoderms.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with 'Equal pay for equal work'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 39**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 39** of the Indian Constitution is a part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) and directs the state to ensure equal pay for equal work for both men and women.
 
• It emphasizes social and economic justice to minimize inequalities in income, opportunities, and status among individuals.
 
• The principle of "Equal pay for equal work" is aimed at eliminating gender discrimination and promoting fairness in employment practices.
 
• Though not enforceable by the courts, Article 39 serves as a guiding principle for policymaking and legislation.
 
• This directive has been reinforced through various labor laws and judicial interpretations in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**

 
 
• DPSPs are enshrined in Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Indian Constitution and aim to establish a welfare state in India.
 
• These principles are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced by the courts but are fundamental in governance.
 
• They act as guidelines for the state to frame laws and policies for the socio-economic development of the country.
 
 
 
• **Equal Pay for Equal Work**
 
 
• The concept is a fundamental aspect of labor rights and is recognized globally under conventions of the International Labour Organization (ILO).
 
• In India, laws such as the Equal Remuneration Act, 1976, uphold this principle by prohibiting gender-based discrimination in wages.
 
• The Supreme Court of India has also upheld this principle in several landmark judgments.
 
 
 
• **Article 14**
 
 
• Article 14 of the Indian Constitution guarantees the right to equality before the law and equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.
 
• While Article 14 focuses on legal equality, Article 39 emphasizes economic and social equality.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Interpretations**
 
 
• In the case of Randhir Singh vs Union of India (1982), the Supreme Court ruled that the principle of "equal pay for equal work" is a constitutional goal under Articles 14, 16, and 39(d).
 
• The judiciary has played a vital role in ensuring the implementation of this principle in labor-related disputes.

• **Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT):**

 
 
• The Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT) was established in **1985** under Article 323A of the Constitution of India.
 
• It was created through the enactment of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985.
 
• The purpose of CAT is to adjudicate disputes and complaints related to the recruitment and conditions of service of persons appointed to public services and posts under the control of the central government or any other authority under its jurisdiction.
 
• CAT is independent of the ordinary judiciary and functions as a specialized tribunal for handling administrative matters.
 
• It has its principal bench in New Delhi, with additional benches in other cities across India for accessibility.

• **Option 2: 1975:**
 
 
• This is incorrect as the idea of tribunals gained prominence in the late 1970s, but CAT was not established until 1985.
 
• The 42nd Amendment to the Constitution (1976) introduced the provision for administrative tribunals, but their actual implementation came much later.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: 1950:**
 
 
• This is incorrect as the concept of specialized administrative tribunals did not exist in India at the time of independence or during the early years of the Constitution.

questions.question: Who among the following appoints the Administrator of a Union Territory without a Legislative Assembly?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The President of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **President of India** appoints the Administrator of a Union Territory (UT) without a Legislative Assembly under Article 239 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Administrator acts as the representative of the President in the Union Territory and exercises powers as delegated by the President.
 
• In Union Territories without Legislative Assemblies (e.g., Lakshadweep, Andaman & Nicobar Islands), the Administrator primarily governs the territory on behalf of the Central Government.
 
• The appointment of the Administrator is done by the President, ensuring that the administration aligns with the policies and interests of the Central Government.
 
• Administrators do not have the same powers as Governors of States, as their role is defined by the Central Government through delegation of authority.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Union Territories:**

 
 
• India has 8 Union Territories, such as Delhi, Puducherry, Chandigarh, Lakshadweep, and others.
 
• Some UTs like Delhi and Puducherry have Legislative Assemblies, while others do not.
 
 
 
• **Article 239 of the Constitution:**
 
 
• This article empowers the President to appoint an Administrator for Union Territories.
 
• The Administrator is responsible for implementing laws and policies in the UT.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Administrator:**
 
 
• The Administrator functions under the direct control of the Central Government.
 
• They are responsible for law and order, governance, and overall administration of the UT.
 
 
 
• **Difference Between Governor and Administrator:**

questions.question: What is the purpose of digitizing evidence collection under Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Improve accuracy and reduce tampering**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Digitizing evidence collection** under the **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (Indian Evidence Act)** aims to **improve accuracy** in the handling of evidence, ensuring that the collected data remains authentic and untampered.
 
• By digitizing evidence collection, the process ensures a **secure chain of custody**, reducing the risk of manual errors or manipulation during the handling of evidence.
 
• **Electronic evidence**, such as digital recordings, documents, or multimedia files, can be timestamped and stored securely, making it more reliable in legal proceedings.
 
• Digitization helps eliminate the risks of **physical damage or loss** of evidence, as digital records are easier to store and retrieve compared to physical copies.
 
• The initiative aligns with the broader goal of modernizing India's legal system by integrating **technology and transparency** into judicial processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (Indian Evidence Act):**

 
 
• The **Indian Evidence Act** was enacted in **1872** and provides the legal framework for the admissibility of evidence in courts.
 
• It lays out rules regarding the **presentation, collection, and validation** of evidence during legal proceedings.
 
• The Act has provisions for handling **electronic evidence**, including emails, digital photographs, and electronic contracts, which are increasingly relevant in the modern era.
 
• Section 65B of the Indian Evidence Act governs the **admissibility of electronic records**, ensuring that they meet specific criteria for authenticity.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Evidence Collection:**
 
 
• Traditional methods of evidence collection often face issues such as **tampering, loss, or delays** in submission.
 
• Manual handling of evidence can lead to human errors, compromising the reliability of the evidence presented in court.
 
• Digitization addresses these challenges by offering **secure and efficient storage and transfer mechanisms**.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of Digitized Evidence Collection:**
 
 
• It ensures better compliance with **legal standards** for admissibility and accuracy.
 
• Digital evidence can be stored in **encrypted formats**, making it secure against unauthorized access or tampering.
 
• Modern tools such as **blockchain** can be used to establish a tamper-proof record of evidence.
 
• Digitization promotes **transparency and trust** in judicial processes by minimizing the scope for manipulation.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Digitization in Legal Systems:**
 
 
• Countries like the **United States** and the **United Kingdom** have adopted digital systems for evidence collection and courtroom procedures.
 
• In India, initiatives such as the **e-Courts project** aim to digitize court records and improve accessibility to legal resources.
 
• The use of **digital forensics** in criminal investigations is increasingly common, allowing authorities to recover and analyze electronic evidence effectively.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Section 65B of the Indian Evidence Act:**

 
 
• This section provides guidelines for the **admissibility of electronic records** as evidence in legal proceedings.
 
• It requires electronic records to be certified, ensuring that they are authentic and reliable.
 
• Courts have emphasized the importance of adhering to Section 65B for the admissibility of digital evidence.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Modernization in India:**
 
 
• The **e-Courts Mission Mode Project** aims to modernize the judiciary by digitizing court records, case management systems, and evidence handling.
 
• These initiatives are part of the **Digital India campaign**, focusing on leveraging technology to improve governance and public services.
 
• Digitization of evidence collection is a key step in achieving faster and more efficient judicial processes.

__
 
• **Every bill after being passed by both houses of Parliament is presented to the President for approval(Article 111)**. There are three alternatives before the president 

 
 
• He may give **approval to the bill**.
 
• He may **withhold his approval for the bill**.
 
• He may r**eturn the bill for reconsideration of the house.**
 
• If the **bill is passed it becomes an act and is a place in the statute book.**
 
 
 
• President enjoys **suspensive veto, absolute veto, pocket veto**.
 
• Article **123 gives power to the President that he can issue ordinance when one of the houses of the Parliament is not in session. The maximum validity of an ordinance is 6 months and 6 weeks**. An ordinance will expire after 6 weeks once both houses of the Parliament are in session.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• The President is the formal head of the executive, legislature and judiciary of India.
 
• He is the **first citizen of India(Article 53).** The idea of the **President is taken from United states of America.**
 
• He is the **commander-in-chief of the Indian Armed Forces.{Article 53(40}.**
 
• The election of President is done by **Single Electoral College,** which consists of the elected members of **both Houses of Parliament and the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of all the States and also of NCT of Delhi and the Union Territory of Puducherry. (Article 54)**
 
• The President shall hold office for a term of **5 years from the date on which he enters upon his office. (Article 56)**.
 
• The oath is taken by the President in the presence of the **Chief Justice of India.** 
 
• If the President violates the law of the Constitution, he may be removed from office by **impeachment (Article 61).**
 
• The President can hand over the **resign to Vice-President**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Under Article 58, a candidate should fulfill the following eligibility conditions to contest the election to the Office of President: -

 
 
• Must be a **citizen of India**,
 
• Must have **completed 35 years of age,**
 
• Must be **eligible to be a member of Lok Sabha.**
 
 
 
• **President has the power to reduce the punishment of a person or can change the nature of punishment(Article 72).**
 
• President has emergency power and they are of three types.:
 
 
• ** National Emergency (Article 352).**
 
• **President’s rule (Article 356 & 365).**
 
• **Financial Emergency(Article 360). **

• The British had sufficient resources both in terms of men and material.
 
• The British soldiers had superior arms and weapons.
